title: {qui} and {que} after a noun (le voisin qui parle, le livre que je lis)
description: Say which person or thing you mean by what it does, or by what someone does to it: {le monsieur qui habite à côté}, {le livre que je lis}.
can_do: Say which person you mean by what they do: {le monsieur qui habite à côté}
Say which thing you mean by what someone does to it: {le livre que je lis}
Say what you and others read: {je lis}, {elle lit}, {j'ai lu}

vocabulary.note: Ends in a nasal vowel, with no n sound: {un voisin}.
vocabulary.example_fr: Le voisin qui habite à côté est très gentil.
vocabulary.example_en: The neighbour who lives next door is very kind.

vocabulary.note: {un copain} is a friend; {mon copain} often means my boyfriend.
vocabulary.example_fr: Hugo, c'est un copain que je vois tous les jours.
vocabulary.example_en: Hugo is a friend I see every day.

vocabulary.note: The polite word for a man: {le monsieur}, {Bonjour, monsieur.} The first syllable sounds like {me}.
vocabulary.example_fr: Le monsieur qui parle à mon voisin, c'est Karim.
vocabulary.example_en: The man talking to my neighbour is Karim.

vocabulary.note: Its forms are in the table: {je lis}, {nous lisons}, {j'ai lu}.
vocabulary.example_fr: Le livre que je lis est très long.
vocabulary.example_en: The book I'm reading is very long.

vocabulary.note: The feminine of {voisin}: now you hear the n.
vocabulary.example_fr: La voisine qui a un chien habite ici depuis un an.
vocabulary.example_en: The neighbour with the dog has lived here for a year.

vocabulary.note: The feminine of {copain}: now you hear the n. {ma copine} often means my girlfriend.
vocabulary.example_fr: C'est une copine que je vois souvent au parc.
vocabulary.example_en: She's a friend I often see at the park.

vocabulary.note: Casual spoken French, used between friends. You need to understand it, not say it.
vocabulary.example_fr: C'est qui, le mec qui parle à Karim ?
vocabulary.example_en: Who's the guy talking to Karim?

vocabulary.note: Spoken French for a thing you don't name. Written French says {chose}.
vocabulary.example_fr: C'est quoi, le truc que tu cherches ?
vocabulary.example_en: What's that thing you're looking for?

concepts.definition: Put {qui} after a noun to say what that person or thing does. {qui} is the subject of the next verb, so no other subject comes after it. The verb agrees with the noun before {qui}: {les enfants qui jouent}, {c'est toi qui viens}. {qui} never shortens before a vowel: {qui a}, {qui habite}.
concepts.example: {La dame qui habite à côté a un chien.} The woman who lives next door has a dog.

concepts.term: {que}: the one someone does it to
concepts.definition: Put {que} after a noun when someone else does the action to it. A subject and a verb come after {que}. English can drop "that" (the film I'm watching), but French always keeps {que}. Before a vowel, {que} becomes {qu'}: {qu'il}, {qu'elle}, {qu'on}.
concepts.example: {C'est le film que je regarde.} That's the film I'm watching.

rows.fr: il lit, elle lit, on lit
rows.en: he reads, she reads, we read

phrases.fr: la voisine qui a un chien

items.instruction: At the window, Léa points out a man in the street to Maya. Join her two sentences with {qui}.
items.shown: C'est le monsieur. Il habite à côté.
items.answer: C'est le monsieur qui habite à côté.

mistakes.answer: C'est le monsieur qu'habite à côté.
mistakes.feedback: {qui} never shortens before a vowel: {qui habite}.

mistakes.answer: C'est le monsieur qui il habite à côté.
mistakes.feedback: {qui} already stands for the man, so drop {il}: {qui habite}.

mistakes.answer: C'est le monsieur que habite à côté.
mistakes.feedback: The man does the living, so use {qui}. {que} needs its own subject after it, as in {que je}.

items.text: Et Karim, c'est le monsieur ___ fait le pain du quartier.
items.gloss: And Karim is the man who makes the neighbourhood's bread.

items.instruction: Maya asks Léa about someone in the street. What does {mec} mean here?
items.shown: C'est qui, le mec qui parle à Karim ?
accept: the guy
a guy
bloke
man
the man
dude

items.text: La vieille dame qui ___ sur le banc, c'est notre voisine.
items.gloss: The old woman reading on the bench is our neighbour.

mistakes.answer: lis
mistakes.feedback: {lis} goes with {je} and {tu}. After {qui}, the verb agrees with {la vieille dame}: {lit}.

items.text: Il a plu ce matin, alors le banc ___ est devant le café est encore humide.
items.gloss: It rained this morning, so the bench in front of the café is still damp.

mistakes.answer: qu'
mistakes.feedback: {qui} never shortens: {qui est}.

mistakes.answer: que
mistakes.feedback: The bench is the subject of {est}, so use {qui}.

items.instruction: Maya picks up a book from Léa's table. Léa tells her about it. Join the two sentences with {que}.
items.shown: C'est le livre. Je lis ce livre.
items.answer: C'est le livre que je lis.

mistakes.answer: C'est le livre je lis.
mistakes.feedback: English can drop "that", but French keeps {que}: {le livre que je lis}.

mistakes.answer: C'est le livre qui je lis.
mistakes.feedback: {je} is the subject: you read the book. Use {que}.

mistakes.answer: C'est le livre que je le lis.
mistakes.feedback: {que} already stands for the book, so drop {le}.

items.text: Prends-le : c'est un livre que j'ai ___ la semaine dernière. Il est super.
items.gloss: Take it: it's a book I read last week. It's great.

mistakes.answer: lis
mistakes.feedback: After {j'ai}, use the participle: {j'ai lu}.

mistakes.answer: lire
mistakes.feedback: After {j'ai}, use the participle: {j'ai lu}.

items.text: Le livre que nous ___ en classe est très long.
items.gloss: The book we're reading in class is very long.

mistakes.answer: lisez
mistakes.feedback: {lisez} goes with {vous}. With {nous}, say {lisons}.

mistakes.answer: lit
mistakes.feedback: After {que}, the verb agrees with its own subject, {nous}: {lisons}.

items.text: Les enfants qui ___ sous l'arbre, ce sont Noé et ses copains.
items.gloss: The children reading under the tree are Noé and his friends.

mistakes.answer: lit
mistakes.feedback: After {qui}, the verb agrees with the noun before it. {les enfants} is plural: {lisent}.

items.instruction: Léa tells Maya about Mme Garnier, the neighbour on the ground floor, and her cat. Join the two sentences with {que}.
items.shown: Voilà le chat. Elle adore ce chat.

mistakes.answer: Voilà le chat que elle adore.
mistakes.feedback: Before a vowel, {que} becomes {qu'}: {qu'elle}.

mistakes.answer: Voilà le chat qui elle adore.
mistakes.feedback: {elle} is the subject: she loves the cat. Use {que}, shortened before the vowel: {qu'elle}.

items.instruction: Léa tells Maya about a woman in the street. Join the two sentences with {que}.
items.shown: C'est la dame. On la voit tous les matins devant le café.
items.answer: C'est la dame qu'on voit tous les matins devant le café.
accept: C'est la dame que l'on voit tous les matins devant le café.

mistakes.answer: C'est la dame qu'on la voit tous les matins devant le café.
mistakes.feedback: {qu'} already stands for the woman, so drop {la}.

mistakes.answer: C'est la dame que on voit tous les matins devant le café.
mistakes.feedback: Before a vowel, {que} becomes {qu'}: {qu'on}.

mistakes.answer: C'est la dame qui on voit tous les matins devant le café.
mistakes.feedback: {on} is the subject: we see the woman. Use {que}, shortened: {qu'on}.

items.question: Léa is looking for Hugo. Which one says "the friend I'm looking for"?

items.situation: On the stairs, Mme Garnier meets Maya for the first time. Ask, as Mme Garnier, whether Maya is the one who comes from Montréal. Start with {C'est toi qui}.
items.answer: C'est toi qui viens de Montréal ?
accept: Bonjour ! C'est toi qui viens de Montréal ?
C'est vous qui venez de Montréal ?

mistakes.answer: C'est toi qui vient de Montréal ?
mistakes.feedback: After {toi qui}, the verb agrees with {toi}, as in {tu viens}: {toi qui viens}.

items.text: Ah, c'est toi ___ je cherche ! Tu veux un gâteau ?
items.gloss: Mme Garnier: Ah, you're the one I'm looking for! Would you like a cake?

items.situation: Back upstairs, Maya is searching Léa's table for something. Ask her what the thing she's looking for is, the way friends say it. Use {truc} and {que}.
items.answer: C'est quoi, le truc que tu cherches ?
accept: Le truc que tu cherches, c'est quoi ?
Qu'est-ce que c'est, le truc que tu cherches ?
C'est quoi, ce truc que tu cherches ?

mistakes.answer: C'est quoi, le truc tu cherches ?
mistakes.feedback: French keeps {que} where English drops "that": {le truc que tu cherches}.

mistakes.answer: C'est quoi, le truc qui tu cherches ?
mistakes.feedback: {tu} is the subject: you are looking for the thing. Use {que}.

items.situation: Maya points at a girl in the street and asks: {C'est qui ?} Tell her it's a friend you see often. Start with {C'est une copine}.
items.answer: C'est une copine que je vois souvent.
accept: C'est une copine que je vois souvent au parc.
C'est une copine qu'on voit souvent.
C'est une copine que je vois tout le temps.

mistakes.answer: C'est une copine qui je vois souvent.
mistakes.feedback: {je} is the subject: you see her. Use {que}.

mistakes.answer: C'est une copine je vois souvent.
mistakes.feedback: French keeps {que} where English drops "that": {une copine que je vois}.

items.situation: Now Maya names the people back. Léa points at the woman with the dog and asks: {C'est qui, elle ?} Answer as Maya, with {la voisine} and {qui}.
items.answer: C'est la voisine qui a un chien.
accept: La voisine qui a un chien.
Elle, c'est la voisine qui a un chien.
C'est la voisine qui a le chien.

mistakes.answer: C'est la voisine qu'a un chien.
mistakes.feedback: {qui} never shortens before a vowel: {qui a}.

mistakes.answer: C'est la voisine que a un chien.
mistakes.feedback: The neighbour has the dog, so she is the subject: use {qui}.

items.situation: Léa asks: {Et Hugo, il est où ?} Maya sees him in front of the café. Answer as Maya. Start with {Le copain que tu cherches}.
items.answer: Le copain que tu cherches est devant le café.
accept: Le copain que tu cherches, il est devant le café.
Le copain que tu cherches est là, devant le café.
Le copain que tu cherches, il est là, devant le café.

mistakes.answer: Le copain qui tu cherches est devant le café.
mistakes.feedback: {tu} is the subject: you are looking for him. Use {que}.

items.text: Bon, je monte. Au revoir, Léa ! Et merci pour le livre ___ tu me donnes !
items.gloss: Maya: Right, I'm going up. Bye, Léa! And thanks for the book you're giving me!

mistakes.answer: qui
mistakes.feedback: {tu} is the subject: Léa gives the book. Use {que}.
